text: On the demand of energy shortage and carbon neutrality, nuclear power plays an indispensable role in modern society. Since the painful Chernobyl and Fukushima accidents, nuclear security has been raising increasing attention of the public. Reactor pressure vessel (RPV), which contains nuclear reactor and suffers from neutron radiation, is one of core security barriers of the reactors [ 1 , 2 ]. The evaluation of its mechanical properties, including impact properties, tensile properties, etc., is vital to the safety evaluation of nuclear power plants, therefore the performance of pre-placed monitoring specimens of RPV steels needs to be evaluated periodically during operation. Due to the radioactivity of specimens after neutron irradiation and limited space inside nuclear plants, small specimens are expected to be developed [3-5] . Nevertheless, the size effects would cause the difference of tested results from different samples and affect the accurate evaluation of mechanical properties, hence it is urgent to figure out the size effects of small specimens of RPV steels, and to normalize the mechanical properties of small specimens to standard ones.

text: As one of major barriers of nuclear reactors, reactor pressure vessels (RPVs) are subjected to neutron irradiation and faced with degradation during operation, therefore their mechanical properties are vital to the safety evaluation of nuclear power plants. Due to the radioactivity of specimens and limited space in the reactors, small tensile specimens are expected to be utilized for tensile property evaluation of RPV steels. However, the size effect would influence the tested tensile results and precise evaluation of mechanical properties of materials. This research is aimed to study the size effects of Chinese RPV steels in detail. It is found that size parameters of tensile specimen will affect the yield behavior, fracture behavior, tensile strength and the elongation, which causes are discussed as well. Moreover, a semi-empirical normalization model is built to normalize the total elongation after fracture of small specimens to the standard industrial specimens, which could make contributes to the normalization of results from different size specimens and serve for the design of small specimen of Chinese RPV steels in industry.

text: There have already been some studies on size-dependent effects of tensile properties of different materials and some rough regularities have been found [6-13] . Total elongation after fracture, δ , as an important parameter to indicate the plasticity of materials, is found to be affected by some parameters of the specimens [14] . For example, significant drops of δ are observed with the increase of original gauge length, L 0 , in pure titanium foils [8] and HY-100 steels [12] , etc. Moreover, thinner specimens always have lower δ than standard specimens [4] . However, synergistic effects caused by multi size parameters and the normalization based on that are still scarce.

text: Yield strength, σ s , and tensile strength, σ b , vital parameters of tensile tests as well, are found to increase with the increase of the thickness and in many materials, there exists a critical thickness, T c , above which the yield strength will not increase anymore [ 9 , 15-17 ]. It is found that for ferrite steels, the critical thickness is about 6 to 15 times of the average grain size, d [13] . However, other studies find that yield strength will significantly increase in micro-leveled thin specimen, including Ni, Cu and Au [19-21] . Besides, it is found that the critical value of tensile strength of Cu also depends on the grain size, and the larger the grain size, the smaller the critical value [18] . Moreover, the aspect ratio (the ratio of thickness and width) on tensile strength of neutron-irradiated modified 316 SS steel and modified dual phase steel has been studied by Kohyama and it is found that there also exists a critical value of the aspect ratio, ranging from 0.1-0.2 for different irradiation states [13] . Some other study finds the aspect ratio of ferritic/martensitic dual phase steel is about 0.18 [6] .

text: The tensile tests were conducted on Instron 5969 mechanical test machine with maximum load of 50 kN. The tensile strain rate was 10 -3 s -1 and the accuracy of loading force was better than 0.5%. The 2620-601 type of the extensometer, which gauge length and accuracy were 12.5 mm and 0.5% respectively, was used to detect the strain of specimens whose L 0 > 12.5 mm. Three sets of gauge length ( L 0 = 15, 10, 6 mm, respectively) were drawn on one specimen to study the influence of gauge length. For smaller specimens whose L 0 < 12.5 mm, non-contact DIC method was used, which could perform stain analysis based on the image of deformation and acquire strain fields of different gauge lengths at one time [24] . The flow charts of DIC procedure were displayed in Fig. 1 c. It included test record, file convert, software installation, GOM correlate platform, strain computation method, DIC parameters setting, DIC processing analysis, calibration and scaling. In the GOM software, the von Mises equivalent strain was used to determine the local strain of the specimens, and based on that, the stress-strain curves could be drawn. Moreover, two sets of gauge lengths ( L 0 = 10 mm and 6 mm, respectively) were set to study the effect of gauge length, whose elongation could be calculated by the GOM software. Based on the parameters of mechanical test machine and its tensile standards, the uncertainty of measurement for strength and elongation is 5 MPa and 0.05%, respectively.

text: [2] and the heat treatment mentioned above, it could be inferred that the microstructure is granular bainite, which is typical microstructures of RPV steels [24-26] and formed by the slow cooling in the core of RPV. Since the thickness of RPV is above 200 mm, the quenching in the core of RPV is quite slow to let bainite transformation happen. Carbon atoms would diffuse from the prior austenite grains, as shown in the green circles in Fig. 2 , and then blocky ferrite and carbon-rich austenite island form. As the materials cool down, the retained austenite, as shown in the red arrows on Fig. 2 , could remain or decompose into mixture and carbides. The XRD analysis in the insert of Fig. 2 presents that it is singlephase body center cubic (BCC) structure and there are no peaks of austenite, indicating that the austenite has already decomposed. text: Interestingly, the yield platform of specimens which thickness is less than 0.5 mm is found to disappear, as shown in the insert of Fig. 4 . Generally, BCC steels containing carbon (C) or nitrogen (N) as interstitial always have yield platform, which upper yield point is driven from the pinning on dislocations of C or N atoms, called Cottrell atmospheres [28] . Meanwhile, the surface would lower the activation energy for diffusion and introduce in image force to the solute atoms, hence drives the diffusion of them. native.text: 5. Conclusion

text: On demand for miniaturization of specimen in nuclear power plants to reduce the radioactivity, size effect on tensile properties of Chinese RPV steels are studied and the influence of the thickness, width, transition arc radius, gauge length on tensile behavior is studied in detail. It is found that yield planform vanishes when T < 0.5 mm, but the yield strength seems to be not affected by the size parameters. Moreover, uniform elongation and tensile strength remain unchanged when the aspect ratio > 0.15, in comparison, post-necking elongation keeps increasing with the increase of the aspect ratio and the decrease of set original gauge length. Finally, based on deformation theory and experimental data, a semi-empirical model is raised to normalize the total elongation of small specimens into standard proportional specimen in industry.
